brief.question: Does eliminating the discarded kinetic block repair the verified lapse defect and retain its necessary fourth-order determinant contribution?
brief.from_parent: The parent proved a nonzero lapse primary/secondary block on vacuum data. Its unit-L2 cutoff-harmonic defect has analytic limit 1/2, not zero; its fixed-low-harmonic second derivative eventually vanishes.
brief.healthy: Exact Schur completion cancels the second lapse derivative in the five specified kinetic cases. Full and factored determinants agree through fourth order. Deliberately omitted high or mixed blocks change coefficients. Increasing auxiliary padding is checked at finite amplitudes; finite residuals do not imply the perturbative identity failed.
brief.noise: Zero completed_curvature and determinant_identity_residual are expected exact results. The determinant is only an axisymmetric angular kinetic block. There is no full scattering amplitude, quantum measure, corner Hilbert space, or reconstruction in this run.
brief.worth_a_flag: A failed exact identity or independent quadrature assertion; a claim that determinant coefficients are physical four-graviton amplitudes; or a claim that vanishing second derivative proves full Dirac closure.
brief.decided: Local CPU, Python standard library only. Preserve the frozen parent experiment. Independent finite-amplitude tests use 60-digit arithmetic and 96/128-node quadrature.
